judge.prompt:
system: You are an evaluation judge. Decide whether one code review finding identifies one specific planted defect. Judge only the defect named, not the location. Return only the requested JSON.
instructions: Input is JSON with "expected", the planted defects at the finding's location (id, file, start, end, defect), and "finding", one reviewer finding (file, start, end, priority, explanation, action).
Return only this JSON object: {"expected":"<id from expected>","verdict":"detects|different-defect","rationale":"<one sentence>"}.
Use "detects" only when the finding describes the same root cause as that planted defect. A finding that shares identifiers, lines or wording but describes another root cause is "different-defect"; then name the closest expected id.
The rationale is one sentence that quotes at least 12 consecutive characters of the finding's explanation or action verbatim inside double quotes.
judge.note: 13 eligible findings, 0 without a valid judge answer; judge cost $0.0244 at Pi catalog prices

The finding identifies the same swallowed write error, stating "If WriteFile fails, Save returns nil" and recommending that the error be returned.
The finding identifies the same unsynchronized concurrent update to total, stating "on the shared variable without synchronization."
The finding identifies the same root cause by stating "The email from the search form is concatenated into the SQL string" and recommends a parameterized query.

The finding identifies the same missing-unlock root cause by stating "Get returns early on a missing key without unlocking the mutex."
The finding states "Comment narrates the obvious code on the next line.", identifying the same redundant comment that restates the assignment.

The finding states "Comment narrates the return statement.", identifying the same redundant comment that restates the return.
The finding identifies the same unsupported promotional claims rather than concrete behavior, describing them as "with unsupported claims" and recommending a verifiable statement of purpose.
